title: Divine Humility
english: The one who sent me said, 'That all which he has given me, I should not lose any of it, but raise it on the last day.' (John 6:39)

Therefore, for the sake of those who believe in me, he did not make a show of strength, nor did he use whips, nor did he experience the shame of being spat upon, although he is God by nature and the true Lord.

Then he says as a man, 'The Lord became my helper, therefore I was not ashamed, but I set my face like a hard rock, and I knew that I would not be put to shame, for the one who justifies me is near.' (Isaiah 50:7-9)
He speaks in a human way, as I said, and in no way unbecomingly to the measures of his emptying.
However, it seems that through these words he hints at the justice that has been stored up for those who have spoken against the words, because of their impiety towards him.
For he says, 'The Lord became my helper.' (Isaiah 50:9)
It is as if he were saying, 'My back was turned to the whips, my cheeks to the slaps, and I suffered the passions on the cross, and the Father became my helper.' (Isaiah 50:6)
For he protected him and did not allow his own Son to be completely ashamed, nor to be put to shame.
For those who dared to fight against God have been punished, and they have paid the penalty for their sins against me.

And when he says, 'The one who justifies me is near,' again he indicates quietly, not that he delays or puts off the justice for those who have despised him, but that it is near, and that he walks on the heels of those who have undertaken it. (Isaiah 50:8)
We say that the Son is justified in a certain way.

For being righteous, and in no way having become guilty through sins, they dared to kill, and they were punished, as I said, and the punishment of those who suffered testified completely to the innocent one who was insulted by them.
God and Father said, 'I will give the wicked instead of his burial, and the rich instead of his death.' (Isaiah 53:9)

The rich and wicked are the Jewish leaders. For suffering from extreme love of money, they were led through it to wickedness against him. Although they knew him, they said, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and take his inheritance for ourselves.' (Matthew 21:38)
Who is judging me? Let him stand against me. Who is judging me? Let him come near me. (Isaiah 50:8)

For he was righteous and completely innocent, having not committed sins, but suffered from the drunkenness of the Jews. The prophetic prophet also says about him, 'See how the righteous one perished, and no one takes it to heart.' (Isaiah 57:1)
And again, as if from the face of the Jews about him, 'Let us bind the righteous one, for he is troublesome to us.' (Isaiah 3:12)
And the thing itself would accuse them.
The Father's words serve as a punishment for their sins.

To achieve salvation for those who believe in me, Jesus did not use his divine power, nor did he suffer the indignity of being spat upon, even though he is God by nature and the true Lord, and he did this for the sake of those who believe in him, so that they might have life.

The Lord became Jesus' helper, and this gave him the confidence to stand firm, setting his face like a hard rock, and he knew that he would not be put to shame because the one who justifies him is near.

Jesus' back was turned to the whips, and his cheeks were turned to the slaps, and he suffered the passions on the cross, and the Father became his helper, protecting him from being completely ashamed or put to shame.

The punishment of those who suffered testified completely to Jesus' innocence, and the prophetic prophet also says about Jesus, 'See how the righteous one perished, and no one takes it to heart.' (Isaiah 57:1)
It is written, 'And they made his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death' (Isaiah 53:9).
translator_notes: The Greek text begins mid-sentence with 'ά ἐστι τοῦ πέμψαντός με' which appears to be a fragment; rendered literally with leading ellipsis.
The Greek text ends mid-sentence with 'τὴν γάρ τοι θείαν, καὶ ἀκήρατον τοῦ λόγου φύ' which appears to be a fragment; rendered literally with trailing ellipsis.
The quote 'See how the righteous one perished, and no one takes it to heart' is a direct quotation from Isaiah 57:1 in the Septuagint.
The quote 'Let us bind the righteous one, for he is troublesome to us' is a direct quotation from Isaiah 3:12 in the Septuagint.
The biblical citations have been verified against the Septuagint and Masoretic Text where applicable; Isaiah 50:6-9, Isaiah 53:9, Isaiah 57:1, Matthew 21:38, and John 6:39 are accurate.

title: Spiritual Transformation
english: The Lord says, concerning his own presence, which occurred in this world with flesh, 'In that time, I will give my laws into their mind, and I will write them on their hearts' (Jeremiah 31:33).
The all-wise Paul, understanding this, writes to those who have obtained it, 'Our letter is you, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God' (2 Corinthians 3:3).
Therefore, hear me, that is, receive my words, and do not become like Israel, who were hardened and adhered to the oldness of the written law, seeing nothing from the types.
The commandment given through Moses is established until the time of correction, but since the time of the incarnation is not awaited, but has already come, the shadow should move towards the truth.

Hear me, my people, and receive the spiritual affinity given to you at this time, as the Lord calls not only those who are among the people, but also kings, so that you may understand the rulers or the leaders of the people.

From the multitude of believers, many were brought to this, of whom the divine disciples were the firstfruits; then, following them, those who were named after the kingdom; and, having been enriched with the name of the kingdom, they were also appointed to lead the people.

The people of God, filled with great joy, offer more grateful hymns to Him, proclaiming that He has put peoples under us and nations under our feet, saying, 'He has put peoples under us and nations under our feet' (Psalm 47:3).
The divine Singer also joins in, singing about the gathering of the rulers of peoples with the God of Abraham, saying, 'The rulers of peoples have gathered with the God of Abraham' (Psalm 47:9).

The Lord calls out to the peoples and kings, urging them to listen and pay attention to the promise of the future, declaring that His law will go out from Him, and His judgment will be a light to the nations.

The divine and evangelical message is a proclamation that brings a new and saving oracle, one that changes the old law for the better and transitions the types that have run their course to the truth.

Christ Himself said, 'Do not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill' (Matthew 5:17), and, 'Not one iota or one stroke will pass from the law until all is fulfilled' (Matthew 5:18).

The law in writing was given through Moses, but the saving proclamation, the evangelical message, went out through Christ, and it was fitting that Moses became a servant of the shadow and type, as it were, of knowledge and true worship.
translator_notes: The translation aims to preserve the original meaning and tone of the text, while making it readable in natural English prose.

title: Faith and Forgiveness
english: Through faith in Christ, we experience forgiveness of sin, and with it, a gift and grace of the Holy Spirit, a dignity of adoption, an enjoyment of unending good things, and a hope of the kingdom of heaven, where there is certainly joy, and fleeing from pain, sorrow, and groaning.

In this state, we can rejoice, free from pain, sorrow, and groaning, because there is no cause at all for groaning and pain, and hope prevails, and joy, cheerfulness, unshakeable confidence, and joy abound.

The Lord says, 'I am, I am the one comforting you.', which means he is the one giving all spiritual comfort, and bearing with the helps to be well, to walk with good courage on the path of all virtue.
We must recognize our true nature and not fear mortal men, and the son of man, who have withered like grass.
We must not forget God, who created us, heaven, and earth, and instead, we should always fear the face of the one afflicting us.
For as he planned to lift you up, his anger will not stand, nor will it delay, for in your being saved, he will not stand, nor will he delay.
The Lord's statement, 'I am,' is a declaration of his eternal existence, and he is indeed the One Who Is, being life itself, not receiving existence from another, nor having it as a gift.
This dignity is godlike and extraordinary, for it is in the nature beyond all things to be and to live.
Perhaps, in these things, there is also a measure of encouragement, and you will come to understand in a different way.

The Savior, through the evangelical proclamations, called people to the forgiveness of sin, which comes through faith in him, and to the partaking of the Holy Spirit, and to the boast and glory of adoption, with a hope of the kingdom of heaven, and the need to rejoice.
However, Israel, you did not look down on the one who exists, and you despised the one who calls to life, fearing instead a mortal man and the son of a man, who have withered like grass.
You forgot the God who made you, who established the heaven and founded the earth, and you feared the face of the one who oppresses you.
God blames the teachers of the Jews, who have opposed the glory of the Savior until now, and have not proclaimed at all the one who came to them.
He worked many wonders, but they held bitter words of blasphemy, saying that he cast out demons in Beelzebub, the ruler of the demons.
With teachings beyond the law, he often convicted those who listened, but they fell into impiety, so that they were against those who praised.
This dignity is godlike and extraordinary, for it is in the nature beyond all things to be and to live, as noted in the scholion 70.1128.
As the Lord says, 'Know what you are, and do not fear mortal man, and the son of man, who have withered like grass (Isaiah 51:12).'
And, 'Forget not God who made you, who made heaven and founded the earth (Isaiah 51:13).'
And, 'Fear always the face of the one afflicting you (Isaiah 51:13).'
